title: Hilbert Schmidt inequalities for positive block matrices

notation.P: XX* in a Gram factorization Delta=[X Y]*[X Y]

background.statement: A finite Hermitian positive semidefinite matrix has a positive square root and a Gram factorization Delta=Z*Z. A nonzero Delta has a factorization with exactly rank(Delta) rows and full row rank.
For U of size m by n and V of size n by m, tr_m(UV)=tr_n(VU); trace is linear and tr(T*T)=sum_ij |T_ij|^2.
A finite sum of nonnegative real numbers is zero exactly when every summand is zero. Thus ||T||HS=0 iff T=0.
If Delta is positive semidefinite and D is compatible, then D*Delta D is positive semidefinite, by testing quadratic forms.
A Gram matrix Z*Z has the same kernel and rank as Z; full row rank of Z implies ZZ* positive definite. Multiplication by isometries preserves the rank and nonzero singular data of the inner factor.

theorems.title: Gram trace identities
assumptions: p and q are positive integers
A is p by p, B is p by q, C is q by q over C
Delta=[[A,B],[B*,C]] is positive semidefinite
Hilbert-Schmidt norms are unnormalized

statement.setup: Delta=[X Y]*[X Y], with X d by p and Y d by q; P=XX*, Q=YY* are d by d. Let a=||A||HS, c=||C||HS, beta=||B||HS^2.

theorems.proof_outline: Expand A=X*X, B=X*Y, C=Y*Y and cycle rectangular traces.

theorems.title: Sum bound and exact Gram gap
assumptions: p and q are positive integers
A is p by p, B is p by q, C is q by q over C
Delta=[[A,B],[B*,C]] is positive semidefinite
Hilbert-Schmidt norms are unnormalized

statement.weighted_gap: s^2 a^2+s^(-2)c^2-2 beta=||sP-s^(-1)Q||HS^2 for every real s>0

theorems.source_relation: Source supporting comparison independently proved with rectangular B.
theorems.proof_outline: Expand the Hilbert-Schmidt square. Alternative: J=diag(I_p,-I_q), S=Delta^(1/2); the gap equals tr(Delta J Delta J)=||SJS||HS^2.

theorems.title: Sharp product bound by reciprocal scaling
assumptions: p and q are positive integers
A is p by p, B is p by q, C is q by q over C
Delta=[[A,B],[B*,C]] is positive semidefinite
Hilbert-Schmidt norms are unnormalized
theorems.proof_outline: If a=0 or c=0, Gram factors give B=0. Otherwise congruence by diag(s^(1/2)I_p,s^(-1/2)I_q) leaves B unchanged and replaces A,C by sA,s^(-1)C. Choose s=sqrt(c/a).

theorems.title: Complete product equality classification
assumptions: p and q are positive integers
A is p by p, B is p by q, C is q by q over C
Delta=[[A,B],[B*,C]] is positive semidefinite
Hilbert-Schmidt norms are unnormalized

statement.zero_case: If a=0 or c=0, then B=0 and product equality always holds.
statement.nonzero_case: If a,c>0, set t=c/a. The following five conditions are equivalent.
equivalent_conditions: Q=tP in any Gram factorization, equivalently P/a=Q/c
There exist 1<=r<=min(p,q), U in C^(p by r), V in C^(q by r), U*U=V*V=I_r, and H=H*>0 in C^(r by r), such that A=UHU*, B=sqrt(t)UHV*, C=tVHV*.

theorems.proof_outline: The optimized Gram gap is zero iff Q=tP. Multiplying out Delta diag(tI,-I) Delta gives the intrinsic identities, whose first trace already yields beta=ac. In a minimal Gram realization, P+Q=(1+t)P>0; take H=P, U=X*P^(-1/2), V=t^(-1/2)Y*P^(-1/2). Conversely the displayed normal form is a PSD factorization and gives equality.
theorems.note: No equality classification from inverse A or inverse C is used; zero cases are separate.

theorems.title: Complete sum equality classification
assumptions: p and q are positive integers
A is p by p, B is p by q, C is q by q over C
Delta=[[A,B],[B*,C]] is positive semidefinite
Hilbert-Schmidt norms are unnormalized

statement.zero_case: If a=0 or c=0, sum equality holds exactly when all three blocks vanish.
statement.nonzero_case: Product equality and a=c; equivalently the normal form in PB3_PRODUCT has t=1.

theorems.proof_outline: Use the Gram square gap and the identity a^2+c^2-2 beta=(a-c)^2+2(ac-beta); the congruence criterion follows from SJS=0 iff the gap is zero and Delta J Delta=S(SJS)S.

theorems.title: Exact normalized Gram deficit
assumptions: p and q are positive integers
A is p by p, B is p by q, C is q by q over C
Delta=[[A,B],[B*,C]] is positive semidefinite
Hilbert-Schmidt norms are unnormalized

statement.interpretation: Near product equality is exactly a small normalized Gram discrepancy; no unproved stability estimate in the original blocks is asserted.

theorems.proof_outline: Expand the squared norm, using ||P/a||HS=||Q/c||HS=1 and tr(PQ)=beta.

theorems.title: Equality rank restrictions and strictness
assumptions: p and q are positive integers
A is p by p, B is p by q, C is q by q over C
Delta=[[A,B],[B*,C]] is positive semidefinite
Hilbert-Schmidt norms are unnormalized

strictness: If Delta is positive definite, both inequalities are strict.
If A and C are positive definite and p!=q, product inequality is strict.
statement.warning: Equal ranks alone, equal diagonal norms alone, or singularity alone do not force equality.

theorems.proof_outline: Read ranks from the normal form. A positive definite (p+q)-square Delta cannot have rank at most min(p,q).

theorems.title: Kernel support and rank bounds
assumptions: p and q are positive integers
A is p by p, B is p by q, C is q by q over C
Delta=[[A,B],[B*,C]] is positive semidefinite
Hilbert-Schmidt norms are unnormalized
theorems.proof_outline: Au=0 implies ||Xu||^2=u*Au=0, hence B*u=Y*Xu=0; apply the same argument to C and use rank-nullity.

theorems.title: Dimension independent optimal constants
assumptions: p and q are positive integers
A is p by p, B is p by q, C is q by q over C
Delta=[[A,B],[B*,C]] is positive semidefinite
Hilbert-Schmidt norms are unnormalized

statement.sum_largest_left_coefficient: The largest universal K in K||B||HS^2<=||A||HS^2+||C||HS^2 is 2.
statement.sum_smallest_right_coefficient: The smallest universal K in ||B||HS^2<=K(||A||HS^2+||C||HS^2) is 1/2.
statement.product_smallest_right_coefficient: The smallest universal K in ||B||HS^2<=K||A||HS||C||HS is 1.
statement.witness: A=C=B=[1]; zero padding gives sharpness for every fixed p,q>=1.
statement.positive_definite_restriction: Constants remain optimal over positive definite block matrices, though equality is impossible; use A=C=[1], B=[1-epsilon], epsilon down to 0.
statement.positive_definite_fixed_dimensions: For each fixed p,q, A=diag(1,epsilon,...), C=diag(1,epsilon,...), B=(1-epsilon)e1 f1* gives eigenvalues 2-epsilon and epsilon repeated p+q-1 times; ratios tend to the sharp constants.

theorems.proof_outline: Evaluate both ratios on the scalar rank-one Gram matrix. For positive definiteness, the scalar perturbed block has eigenvalues epsilon and 2-epsilon.

theorems.title: Positive compression comparison
assumptions: K is positive semidefinite n by n over C
E is n by p and F is n by q
n,p,q positive integers

statement.equality: Use PB3_PRODUCT and PB3_SUM with X=K^(1/2)E, Y=K^(1/2)F.

theorems.proof_outline: Apply the positive-block theorem to [E F]*K[E F].

counterexamples.claim_refuted: Positive definite A,C alone imply either block inequality.
Some finite universal constant gives either homogeneous upper bound for arbitrary Hermitian blocks.
counterexamples.certificate: Both right sides vanish and ||B||HS^2=1; v=(1,-1), v*Delta v=-2

counterexamples.claim_refuted: Scalar entrywise two-by-two principal PSD tests suffice.
counterexamples.certificate: All |B_ij|^2=A_ii C_jj=1, but ||B||HS^2=4>2=||A||HS||C||HS; v=(1,1,-1,-1), v*Delta v=-4

counterexamples.claim_refuted: For PSD Delta with ||A||HS=||C||HS, BB*<=A^2 in Loewner order.
counterexamples.certificate: A^2-BB*=diag(12,-3) is indefinite; Delta has the Gram factorization in E08.
